analyzed_vuln.description: The bug is a stale-pointer read during optimization: `VariableReference::constantPropagate` unconditionally dereferences `this->variable()->initialValue()`, but the `Variable` (or its declaration/value storage in the pooled IR) can already be poisoned/invalidated after prior CFG simplification/mutation. `Variable::initialValue()` (`skia/src/sksl/ir/SkSLVariable.cpp:15`) returns `fDeclaration->value().get()` without validating lifetime, so constant propagation reads from poisoned pool memory, producing the ASan use-after-poison.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered via `sksl2pipeline` when compiling malformed/minimized SkSL like `void a(){if(2>2)int a;a;}`. During `Compiler::optimize -> scanCFG -> simplifyExpression`, constant propagation runs on a `VariableReference` to a local variable whose declaration/initializer state has become invalid due to earlier CFG dead-code transformations. The pass then calls `variable()->initialValue()` and reads poisoned pooled memory (8-byte read in `unique_ptr::get`).
